cards.title: Footprints in wet cement
cards.body:
Everything you post, like, comment on or get tagged in adds to your **digital footprint**: the trail you leave online.

Like footprints in wet cement, it can set hard. Posts get screenshotted, shared and saved, even after you delete them. That's not a reason to stop posting: it's a reason to **choose what you share**.

cards.title: What to keep private
cards.body:
Some details help strangers find you, or pretend to be you ([[identity theft]]). Keep these off public posts and profiles:

- your **home address** and **phone number**
- your **school**, including a uniform or badge in photos
- your **full name with your birthday**
- **where you are right now**: post holiday photos **after** you get home
- **passwords, codes**, and photos of tickets or ID cards
- answers to **security questions**, like your first pet's name or the street you grew up on

That goes for **usernames** too: `SkyDiver_77` is safer than your real name, school or birth year.

A good test: would you be OK with a stranger, a future teacher or a future boss seeing it?

cards.prompt: Fine to share, or keep it private?

items.label: A photo of your pet (no name tag)
A selfie in your school uniform
Holiday photos while you're still away
Your phone number in your bio

cards.explanation: Interests and things you make are fine to share. Your **school**, **address**, **phone number** and **where you are right now** help strangers find you, so keep them private.
cards.hint: For each one, ask: could a stranger use this to find me, or to pretend to be me?
cards.nudge: Details that show where you live, go to school or are right now are the ones to keep private.

cards.prompt: A fun quiz is going around on social media.

steps.text: **"Find your pop star name! It's your first pet's name plus the street you grew up on. Share yours below!"** What do you do?

choices.text: Share it. It's just a bit of fun
choices.consequence: Pet names and streets are common **security questions**, so sharing them helps someone reset your accounts.
Nothing personal shared. Quizzes like this are sometimes made to collect exactly those answers.

cards.explanation: "Fun" quizzes can collect the answers to **security questions** (your first pet, your street, your school). Enjoy them without posting the answers.
cards.hint: Think about where else you might have been asked for your first pet's name or your street.

cards.title: Privacy settings
cards.body:
Every app has **privacy settings**. A few worth checking:

- **Private account:** only people you approve see your posts.
- **Who can message you:** friends only, not everyone.
- **Location sharing:** off, unless it's with family you trust.
- **Tag review:** you approve photos before they show on your profile.

Apps sometimes change settings in updates, so check them again every now and then.

If someone online makes you uncomfortable, you can **block** and **report** them in the app, and tell a trusted adult. You won't be in trouble.

cards.prompt: Match each setting to what it does.

pairs.right: Only approved followers see your posts
Nobody can see where you are right now
You approve photos you're tagged in

cards.explanation: A **private account** limits who sees posts, **friends-only messages** keep strangers out of your inbox, **location off** hides where you are, and **tag review** lets you choose which photos of you appear.
cards.hint: Think about what each setting controls: your posts, your messages, your location or your photos.
cards.nudge: Two are about who can see things, one is about who can contact you, and one is about photos other people post.

cards.prompt: Why is it smart to post holiday photos **after** you get home?

options.text: It doesn't tell people you're away right now
Photos look better when edited at home
options.nudge: Photo quality isn't the reason. Think about what the post tells people about where you are.
Likes aren't the reason. Think about who might learn that your home is empty.

cards.explanation: Posting while you're away tells people **where you are, and that you're not home**. Share the photos once you're back.
cards.hint: The lesson said to keep "where you are right now" private.

cards.prompt: Someone you don't know in real life has been messaging you in a game. They're really friendly.

steps.text: After a few days they ask: **"What school do you go to? Send me a photo of you!"** What do you do?

choices.text: Send it. They've been really nice
choices.consequence: Being friendly online doesn't show who someone really is. A school and a photo help a stranger find you.

choices.text: Don't send anything, block and report them, and tell a trusted adult
choices.consequence: That's exactly right. You're not in trouble, and telling someone keeps you and others safe.

cards.explanation: Keep your school, photos and location away from people you only know online, however friendly they seem. **Block, report and tell a trusted adult**: you won't be in trouble.
cards.hint: Look back at what to keep private. Who could help you if something online feels off?

cards.prompt: Is each username **safe**, or does it **give too much away**?
cards.explanation: A good username says nothing about who you are. `Mia_Jones_Brisbane2013` gives a full name, a city and a birth year, and `Liam_at_Hillside_High` gives a name and a school.
cards.hint: Look for a real name, a school, a place or a birth year inside each username.
cards.nudge: Fun made-up words are safe. A real name, school, town or birth year gives too much away.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Your **digital footprint** is everything about you online, and it can last.
- Keep your **address, phone number, school, location right now** and passwords private.
- Quizzes can collect **security question** answers.
- Check your **privacy settings**: private account, friends-only messages, location off, tag review.

Next: what your apps can see, and staying safe on public Wi-Fi.
